All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each SKILL.md's final-step `--ac` block replaced with concrete skill-session deliverable ACs (4 per skill for skills with multiple deliverables; 3 for simpler skills).
2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — skill-session ACs: plan approved, children created, ACs traceable.

# implement.py parent ignores the do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child

relocated-from:AH-0MUWGZ7UH007NBT4 (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

discovered-from:AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` selects the next startable child purely from status, dependency order and `sortIndex`, so a child tagged `do-not-delegate` is claimed and started on every dispatch — the epic then livelocks on the one child that must not be automated, and its genuinely startable siblings are never reached.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers** (herdr downtime worker running `implement.py parent <epic>` / `drive <epic>` unattended):
  *As the dispatcher, when the lowest-sorting remaining child is `do-not-delegate`, I want it reported as guarded and skipped so the next genuinely startable sibling runs — or a clean "no startable child" stop — instead of a claim/worktree churn cycle every cycle.*
- **Operators driving an epic manually:**
  *As an operator, I want the parent report to tell me which child is guarded and why nothing started, so I do not have to abort a wrongly-claimed child before the real work can proceed.*
- **Maintainers:**
  *As a maintainer, I want the guard covered by a regression test with the exact shape that broke (guarded child lowest `sortIndex`, open startable siblings), so the selection rule cannot silently regress.*

## Observed failure

AI_Hell epic `AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J`: child **Evaluate switching to runtime generation when ToneForge is Runtime-ready (AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6)** carries the `do-not-delegate` tag and must stay unstarted until the external item **Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback) (TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0)** is terminal. `implement.py parent` started it anyway, on every re-run, leaving the three startable siblings (Thruster hum Tone.js shim, Update audio documentation, Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene) unreached until an operator aborted the guarded child manually. The previous session recorded the same gap in a comment on 2026-10-05T21:17Z.

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_classify_child()` (line ~872) returns only `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` / `implement` — `tags` are never consulted anywhere in the module (`grep do-not-delegate` → zero hits in the repo).
- The live selection path is the `phase_parent()` child loop (line ~5830); `_next_child_to_implement()` (line ~963) is **not called by production code** — only by tests. A fix limited to `_next_child_to_implement()` would not change behaviour.
- `wl_show_children()` (line ~473) already returns each child's `tags` array from `wl show <id> --children --json` (verified against live data) — honouring the tag needs **no** extra `wl` subprocess and no schema change.
- The current waiting branch (line ~5935) reports only `blocked_children` and the message "blocked by non-terminal siblings or another agent holds them" — a guarded child would be mis-described by it.
- `phase_drive()` (line ~6656) consumes `parent.next_child` and stops when it is absent, passing `blocked_children` through.
- `wl` itself already treats `do-not-delegate` as a guard rail (`worklog` `delegate-helper.js`): it refuses to hand such an item to an automated agent unless `--force`. `implement.py` selecting that child for an automated implement session is the same delegation, so the semantics align. 33 items in this store currently carry the tag.

## Desired change

Treat a `do-not-delegate`-tagged child as **not startable by automatic parent recursion**, report it distinctly, and leave explicit invocation as the documented override.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Guarded classification.** A child whose `tags` contain `do-not-delegate` classifies as a dedicated guarded action (e.g. `skip-do-not-delegate`) via `_classify_child()`, matched case- and whitespace-insensitively and safe against a missing/`None` `tags` field; `_next_child_to_implement()` skips it in the same way it skips terminal children.
- [ ] **AC2 — Parent never starts a guarded child.** `phase_parent()` neither claims (`status=in_progress`) nor creates a worktree for a guarded child. It records `action: "skipped-do-not-delegate"` in `children_processed`, lists the ids in a `guarded_children` report field, and still starts the next startable sibling in dependency/`sortIndex` order.
- [ ] **AC3 — No premature advance, distinct waiting report.** When the only non-terminal children left are guarded, the parent is **not** advanced to `completed`/`in_review`, no `next_child` is reported, and the message names the guarded children and the tag (not the dependency-blocked wording). Re-running the phase is idempotent: no claim, no worktree, no status change, same report.
- [ ] **AC4 — Drive parity.** `phase_drive()` spawns no child session for a guarded child and surfaces `guarded_children` (plus an explicit "guarded by `do-not-delegate`" message) rather than a misleading "blocked or held" stop.
- [ ] **AC5 — Explicit override unchanged.** Direct `implement.py start <child>`, `finish <child>` and `drive <child>` on a guarded item continue to work — only automatic selection inside parent recursion is gated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Regression tests.** Tests cover the classifier (guarded / unguarded / case-and-whitespace variants / missing tags), a mixed parent set (guarded child with the lowest `sortIndex` plus open siblings → sibling starts, guarded reported), an all-guarded parent (no advance, guarded message, idempotent re-run), and `drive` (no session spawned). Tests fail before the change and pass after.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` guard list documents the `do-not-delegate` skip, and the affected docstrings (`_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`) plus any `docs/dev/` reference describe the new action and report field.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Automatic selection only.** `do-not-delegate` guards parent recursion; naming the child explicitly is the documented override (mirrors `wl delegate --force`).
- **Guarded ≠ terminal.** A guarded child must never count toward parent advancement.
- **Do not widen scope** to the stale-worktree-branch half of the superset item (its AC3/AC4) — that is a separate fix.
- **No new subprocess per child:** rely on the `tags` already present in `wl show --children` output.
- **Additive report shape:** existing fields (`children_processed`, `blocked_children`, `next_child`) keep their meaning; `guarded_children` is new.
- **No behaviour change** for terminal, in-progress or dependency-blocked classifications, and no change to the deterministic topological ordering.
- Changes affect every project once `scripts/install_pi.sh` is re-run, so the change must be built, tested and shipped on `dev` before installation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — add a `DO_NOT_DELEGATE_TAG` constant and tag helper, a `skip-do-not-delegate` branch in `_classify_child()`, skip-and-report handling in the `phase_parent()` child loop, a `guarded_children` report field plus its waiting message, and `phase_drive()` passthrough; update affected docstrings.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` — new regression tests (classifier, mixed parent, all-guarded, drive no-spawn).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py` — the existing parent-recursion suite (root `tests/`, not `skill/implement/tests/`); extend with the guarded-child case if a shared fixture is the cheaper fit. Sibling suites: `tests/test_implement_parent_loop.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py`.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — "Guards (deterministic, in `phase_parent`)" list entry for the `do-not-delegate` skip.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reference documentation of the new classification action and `guarded_children` report field.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `do-not-delegate` means "no unattended agent may pick this up", matching `wl`'s own delegate guard rail; the tag is already used with that meaning in this store.
- **Risk (over-blocking):** the tag is present on 33 items, most completed/deleted; the guard must only ever apply to *non-terminal* children inside parent recursion, so an already-terminal tagged child keeps its existing skip-terminal handling and is not re-reported as guarded.
- **Risk (silent stall):** skipping a guarded child without an explicit stop reason would look like the "all children held" case; the distinct message plus `guarded_children` is the mitigation.
- **Risk (ordering regression):** the topological sort and `sortIndex` tie-breaks must be untouched — only classification changes.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the stale-worktree-branch defect in SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G and the readiness-ordering defect in SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J are separable; any extra improvement spotted here is recorded as a follow-up item, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G** — *implement.py parent ignores do-not-delegate and leaves stale worktree branches* (`intake_complete`, open). Superset item: its AC1/AC2 describe exactly this behaviour (dedicated guarded classification, parent-loop skip, explicit-start override) alongside a stale-branch fix. Already carries an effort/risk estimate (Small / Medium) and a find-related report; the superset's intake note records this item as "the do-not-delegate subset to be absorbed on resolution".

Per the instruction recorded on this item when it was relocated — *"Retained separately to preserve the original report; close as duplicate/absorbed once SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G is resolved"* — this item is **not** implemented independently. It is tracked and linked to the superset item; when SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G lands and delivers the `do-not-delegate` skip, this item is closed as absorbed (`Duplicate of SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G`).

## Problem

The implement skill's Step 9 'belt-and-suspenders' post-push verification (/skill:test against the dev checkout) can resolve to a **cache hit and execute zero fresh tests**, while still looking like a green verification.

Observed end-to-end on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK:
1. implement.py finish runs the full suite (changed-scope, then --scope full) **inside the worktree**, stores green entries keyed by git state + scope in the per-repo test cache (2h TTL).
2. implement.py pushes from the worktree. In this repo the pre-push hook is a worklog-sync hook that exits 0 for worktrees (line ~80) — no test execution happens at push time.
3. The skill then says run /skill:test post-push. Because the cache key is git state + scope only, the main checkout's lookup at the same commit hits the entry stored by the finish gate. Both suite commands returned CACHED exit=0 — the final verification ran nothing.
4. Worse: the worktree environment can differ from the main checkout in ways the cache cannot see — on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK the core submodule failed to clone in the worktree ('transport file not allowed') and was populated manually; node_modules is symlinked. A green run recorded in the worktree is not proof the canonical checkout passes.

## Desired behaviour

- The post-push verification step must either (a) execute a genuinely fresh run against the canonical checkout when the push originated in a worktree (or when env differs), or (b) be made explicitly targeted for narrow changes (--scope changed --force) instead of a bare /skill:test that is cache-servable.
- The cache key should include enough environment/worktree identity that a worktree-recorded run cannot satisfy a main-checkout verification, OR implement.py finish should record whether the push came from a worktree so the post-push step knows to force a refresh.
- Keep fast iteration cheap: for narrow, well-covered changes, a forced changed-scope run is acceptable post-push evidence; reserve forced full runs for broad/refactor changes or environment drift (submodules, node_modules).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After implement.py finish pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification on the main checkout executes a fresh run (it cannot be served from the cache entry recorded inside the worktree) for the affected scope.
- AC2 — A bare /skill:test post-push no longer silently returns 'green' from a cache populated by an in-worktree finish gate without executing: either the step force-refreshes, or the implement skill's Step 9 is updated to specify an explicit scope/force invocation (and documents when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key (or its consumer logic in run_tests.py / implement.py) captures worktree-vs-main-checkout identity (e.g. git common dir, worktree path, or submodule status) so an in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted post-push runs (--scope changed --force) remain the default for narrow changes; the full forced suite runs only when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (submodule/node_modules) is detected.
- AC5 — Documented in implement SKILL.md Step 9 (and audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant) with the exact commands; regression test in tests/ where the cache layer is tested.

## Constraints

- Do not break existing 2h-TTL caching for the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification — it still needs to query cached full runs at the same commit.
- Pre-existing framework items may partially intersect: SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe), SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard + push timeout). Reconcile rather than duplicate.
- Target files (from the live symlink tree /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills -> /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill): skill/test_cache.py (cache key), skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py (scope/force), skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (push origin record / verification step), skill/implement/SKILL.md (Step 9 wording), skill/audit/SKILL.md (F3/F4 notes if needed).

## Evidence

- Final /skill:test on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: both suites reported CACHED exit=0 scope=full, i.e. no fresh execution.
- Worktree push: pre-push hook exits 0 for worktrees (saw line ~80 'exit 0' in .git/hooks/pre-push); submodule 'core' failed to clone in the worktree and was populated manually.

## Users

  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.

  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try

      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed

      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no

      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).

      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /

# Finish gate: test the tree the commit produces, and prove every verdict's provenance

## Objective

Make `implement.py finish`'s test gate validate the exact tree the commit
will produce, and make every gate verdict self-describing (which tree ran,
whether it came from cache). A green gate must never again be produced by a
suite run against a different tree or by a stale cached result.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` runs the test gate **before** it stages and commits
(`git_commit` performs `git add -A` afterwards). Suite tests that key off the
**tracked** file set (`git ls-files`) therefore cannot see files the commit is
about to add, and the gate can report a green full-scope run for a tree that
is red the moment the commit lands. The false green is silent: the report says
"full scope, success", so no agent looks further, and the tree stays red at
the push, in CI, and for the next agent.

Observed on ContentCreator work item **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** (Ep 1 of *Inside
the Content Creation Suite*):

- `implement.py finish` reported `{"tooling": "suite", "scope": "full",
  "success": true}` and pushed commit `9c88625c`.
- A full-suite run on the same tree immediately after reported **2 failed**,
  both caused by the newly added files:
  - `test_no_podcast_episode_content_tracked_outside_documented_leftovers` —
    `podcasts/ep1-why-use-it/*` were not yet in `git ls-files`, so the
    allowlist guard passed pre-commit and failed post-commit.
  - `test_registry_documents_match_on_disk_documents` — the wiki registry was
    stale for the new synthesis page. This test reads **on-disk** files, not
    `git ls-files`, so untracked-invisibility cannot explain its false pass.
- The item was re-finished (`9f3a1f6c`) after fixing the allowlist and
  rebuilding the metadata; the suite was green at that commit
  (`2765 passed, 16 skipped`). The defect is the false green, not the fix.

Origin record: **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** (ContentCreator worklog) — full intake
brief, investigation trail, and evidence.

## Investigation findings (from the origin intake)

Two mechanisms are supported; both must be closed:

1. **Untracked-file invisibility (proved).** `git_commit` stages *after* the
   test step, and the suite runs against the loose working tree. Anything
   using `git ls-files` semantics cannot see the commit's new files.
2. **Verdict may not correspond to a suite run at the gate's tree (root
   cause to pin).** Surviving cache evidence: the nearest green full-suite
   entry in the shared `.worklog/cache` (08:53, state `8e9c3ea7…`) collected
   **2751** tests, i.e. the dev tree before the episode work's test files
   existed; the post-commit red run (10:56, `f73d063e…`) collected **2781**,
   matching the committed tree. The gate's own per-worktree cache was deleted
   with the worktree, so the exact entry served cannot be recovered. Because
   the parity test reads disk, untracked-invisibility alone cannot explain its
   pass: the gate either executed against a different checkout/state or served
   a cached result recorded for a different tree.

## Desired change

1. **Temporary-index gate (operator-approved option A).** Before the gate's
   test step: copy the real index to a temp file, apply the change set to the
   copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the suite with
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
   `git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
   index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds; on failure the temp
   index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.
   `GIT_INDEX_FILE` is currently **not** in `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`
   (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`), so it survives the runner's env scrub —
   this must be asserted by a regression test so a future scrub addition
   cannot silently break the fix.
2. **Verifiable verdicts.** The gate's report must state (a) the tree the
   suite ran against (worktree path + git fingerprint) and (b) whether the
   result was served from the cache. A cached verdict is acceptable only when
   its fingerprint is the would-be-commit tree's fingerprint; otherwise the
   suite must run.

Rejected: stage-then-test with unstage-on-abort (mutates the real index,
fragile restore); `git status --porcelain`-clean assertion only (demands a
clean tree and still does not test the commit's file set).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Gate tests the would-be commit tree:** a change set that adds a file rejected by a tracked-file guard (`git ls-files` semantics) fails the finish gate, with the failing test named, instead of reporting a green full-scope pass. Reproduced through the finish-gate entry point.
- [ ] **The gate proves its verdict:** the report records the tree it ran against (worktree path + fingerprint) and whether the result came from cache; no green verdict is accepted for a state whose suite has not run (stale/foreign cache entries must miss).
- [ ] **Abort leaves the tree unchanged:** on gate failure there is no partial commit, no residual staging, and the temporary index is removed.
- [ ] **Cache determinism:** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` passes through the test skill's env scrub into child git commands (regression test), and the gate's cache key reflects the would-be-commit tree, not the loose working tree.
- [ ] **Existing green runs unaffected:** a clean change set passes exactly as today with a single gate suite execution (no duplicate run).
- [ ] **Parity false pass explained:** the regression work reproduces the disk-reading parity case at the finish-gate entry point and records the root cause (wrong checkout / stale cache / metadata lag before staging) in this work item.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** the framework suites pass — `skill/implement/tests/`, `skill/test/tests/`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`, plus the repository full suite at the dev-push gate.
- [ ] **Documentation:** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (finish gate semantics, verdict provenance), `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (cache fingerprint / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` contract) updated. CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship skill and excluded.
## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: no default bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc.);
  guard ownership (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`) and the nested-run stand-down
  contract stay intact.
- ✗ One suite execution per gate verdict on a clean change set.
- ✗ The changed-scope development gate stays the fast path; the full suite
  stays the dev-push integration gate.
- ✗ Implemented in this repository (framework); do not edit the global install
  directly.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` test step,
  `git_commit`, `_run_resolved_suite` / `_run_guarded_suite`, gate report keys.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state` / `run_cached` / `cache_dir`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`, env construction
  (`subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides`).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_guard_ownership.py`,
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py` —
  regression-test homes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** a temporary index changes *staged* status, which may surprise
  tests asserting on working-tree state beyond `git ls-files` (e.g.
  `git ls-files --error-unmatch` in ContentCreator's
  `test_implement_state_gitignore.py`). Mitigation: re-verify such tests in
  the regression work and document the semantics.
- **Risk:** two cache entries per state (loose vs staged fingerprint);
  accepted — correctness over hit ratio.
- **Assumption:** the parity false pass shares the gate-to-tree mismatch
  cause rather than a metadata-lag-only cause; the reproduction settles it.
- **Cross-repo note:** project-level fallout (ContentCreator's missing
  pre-push full-suite gate) is tracked separately in the OSL worklog, not
  here.

## Related work

- **OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2** — origin record and intake brief (ContentCreator).
- **OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA** — work item whose first finish produced the false
  green (`9c88625c`, corrected by `9f3a1f6c`).
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — live-repo guard vs pre-push gate duration and
  implement push timeout.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H**, **SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q** — guard ownership.
- **OSL-0MUHNOJ8E002YKUO** — accidental `.implement_state.json` tracking via
  the same `git add -A` staging surface.

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem statement

`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` never matches a PSI line, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered `n/a` ("unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)") even when `/proc/pressure/*` is present and readable — three of the twelve before-table metrics are dead weight and the pressure analysis in Step 2 can never fire on stall data.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before table to show the kernel's stall percentages so I can tell CPU contention from memory or I/O starvation without guessing."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want the numeric pressure value in the metrics dict so `pressure_analysis.analyze_pressures()` can surface a real pressure with contributors instead of skipping the metric."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want PSI parsing covered by verbatim-content unit tests so a wrong fixture can't mask the bug again."

## Evidence (verified)

Re-verified on this host (16-core Ubuntu, 2026-10-23): all three collectors return `None` while PSI is readable.

```
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=84206005618   # /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=64384303      # /proc/pressure/memory (some)
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=35437059      # /proc/pressure/memory (full)
some avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=398915844     # /proc/pressure/io (some)
full avg10=0.05 avg60=0.11 avg300=0.10 total=270870893     # /proc/pressure/io (full)
```

Original discovery run (2026-10-21) showed genuine CPU `some` pressure of `avg10=11.58` alongside load 11.92 on 16 cores — real signal was thrown away.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):        # never true — lines start with "some " / "full "
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])    # tokens are avg10=<v> etc., not bare numbers
return None
```

Two independent defects: the prefix test can never match, and the value token needs `split("=")` (not whitespace index 1). The existing unit test passes only because it feeds a fabricated two-line fixture (`some:stuff` followed by `avg10  60.00 60.00 60.00`) that matches the buggy parser rather than real kernel output.

## Desired change

1. `_read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None` parses real PSI output, returning the `avg10` stall percentage of the requested `some`/`full` line; returns `None` when the file is missing/empty/unparsable or the requested line is absent.
2. `pressure_specs` gains a per-metric line selector (decided: **`cpu` → `some`; `memory` → `full`; `io` → `full`**) so the semantic choice is explicit in code.

# Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted

## Goal

When a child's failing `finish` exhausts its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), re-fetch the child via `wl show` and classify it with the existing `_is_terminal_child` check: if terminal, record it as done and continue — never finish, reset, or re-spawn it.

## Problem statement

A finish failure can occur after the child actually reached a terminal state (e.g. push succeeded but a post-push gate step failed). Today drive treats every `finishing_failed` as chain-fatal, so a child that is genuinely `completed`/`in_review`/deleted still stalls the whole epic and blocks parent advancement — even though terminal children are already handled in the classification (`_classify_child` returns `skip-terminal` before the worktree/finish path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC2: 2. **Terminal-state reconciliation.** When a child's `finish` has exhausted its attempts (or the child is found terminal at any point), drive re-fetches the child via `wl show`: if the child is terminal (`completed`/`done` status or `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted), it is recorded as done (`ok`), never reset, and drive continues to the next actionable child.
- 1. After a child's finish-attempt bound is reached, drive re-fetches the child via `wl show` and applies the existing `_is_terminal_child` classification (`completed`/`done` status, `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted `deletedBy` set) — AC2 of the parent.
- 2. A terminal child is recorded as done in `children_driven` with a distinguishing `terminal-reconciled` outcome (never `failed`), and drive continues to the next actionable child — it is never `finish`ed, reset, or re-spawned.
- 3. The reconciled per-child entry carries evidence (child status/stage, failure summary) — AC4 of the parent.
- 4. Regression coverage: terminal children are never touched by the recovery path; `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test — AC5 of the parent.
- 5. Unit tests with injectable `parent_runner` cover both finish-failure → terminal reconciliation and the terminal-child regression.
- 6. Reconciliation adds no latency on the happy path (re-fetch runs only on the slow finish-failure path).
- 7. Full test suite green for the changed scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` reconciliation branch; reuse `_is_terminal_child` (~786) and `_classify_child` (~807).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new reconciliation + regression tests (fixtures from the harness feature).

## Constraints

- This feature only reads child state and records truthful results; the status/worktree reset mutation belongs to the sibling reset feature.
- Cross-link rather than absorb SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (timeout path reconciliation) — this feature covers only the `finishing_failed` path.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Depends on the bounded-attempts feature; blocks the reset-for-retry feature.

# Reset non-terminal child for clean retry (no livelock)

## Goal

A non-terminal child whose `finish` exhausted its bound is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) — with a recorded audit comment; drive then continues so the next loop iteration starts a fresh session for that child. `parent_advanced` becomes `true` only when every child is terminal.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` failure resets the child status to `open` but leaves the worktree dirty (build/tests red on abandoned WIP). The next `parent` run classifies the dirty worktree as "has changes" and re-runs the identical failing `finish` — the exact unbounded loop that livelocked epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX for 29+ drive runs. Recovery must deterministically break that loop and recover to a clean startable state without silently discarding the child owner's WIP.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC3: 3. **Non-terminal recovery, no livelock.** A non-terminal child whose `finish` failed is reset to a clean startable state — item status `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path and its worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`) with a recorded comment naming the failure reason — after which drive continues and the next iteration starts a fresh session for it. `parent_advanced` reflects the true state (false only when non-terminal/blocked work genuinely remains). Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario must terminate with the epic advancing.
- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC4: 4. **Truthful report.** Per-child `children_driven` entries / failure reasons distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` (with evidence: child status/stage, failure summary).
- 1. When a non-terminal child's finish attempts are exhausted, drive performs the explicit recovery mutation: child status → `open` via the shared `StatusLifecycle` path, and the child's own worktree reset to the parent-branch HEAD (`git reset --hard <parent-branch>` + `git clean -fd`), gated on worktree-isolation checks so the reset only ever touches the child's own worktree, never the main checkout — AC3 of the parent.
- 2. An audit comment is recorded on the child naming the failure reason, the finish-attempt count, and the reset performed — WIP is never discarded silently (AC3, constraints).
- 3. After the reset, drive continues instead of breaking on the exhausted bound: the next loop iteration starts a fresh session for that child (session-attempt accounting continues).
- 4. Reset never runs for terminal children (regression guard from the reconciliation feature remains green).
- 5. Truthful per-child reporting: `children_driven` entries distinguish `finished`, `terminal-reconciled`, and `reset-for-retry` with evidence (child status/stage, failure summary); `parent_advanced` is `false` only while real non-terminal/blocked work remains — AC3/AC4 of the parent.
- 6. Reproducing the AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX scenario (fake runner always `finishing_failed`, non-terminal child, dirty worktree) terminates within the loop bound with the epic advancing — unit-tested (AC3).
- 7. Full test suite green for the changed scope.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` reset branch; new worktree-reset helper (git worktree mechanics, isolation-gated); reuse `_is_worktree`/`_git_path_has_changes`/`_has_worktree_changes` (read-only).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `StatusLifecycle.update_status` for the status-reset path.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — reset+continue tests with fake runner + in-repo git worktree fixture (ScratchRepo pattern from existing implement tests).

## Constraints

- Reset is explicit, bounded, and always commented; use `git reset --hard <parent-branch>` only inside the child's own worktree; never `git clean` on shared paths (Risk R1 of the parent).
- Recovery mutation is a work-item mutation → runs only while the item is claimed (StatusLifecycle guard), and only touches the child's own worktree.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC3, AC4).
- Depends on bounded-attempts + reconciliation features; feeds the docs feature.
- Do NOT absorb AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81 (behind-only worktree mis-detection that feeds the same `has_changes → finish` path) — cross-link only.

# Verified reversible local-dev sync + ancestry assertion

Implementation feature of parent SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY. Makes the shared
local-`dev` fast-forward verified and reversible (parent AC1) and adds the
post-push ancestry assertion (parent AC2), so a `finish` can never report
success for a commit that did not land on `origin/dev`. Depends on the lock
(F2) serialising the window and on the regression suite (F1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — local-dev sync is remote-verified. The pre- and post-push local dev sync.
- AC2 — ancestry assertion. After the push, `finish` asserts its own commit.
- Pre- and post-push local `dev` updates only fast-forward to a commit that
  is already on `origin/dev` (or refuse loudly, naming the ref/hash, when
  local `dev` has moved since the worktree base). Local `dev` is never left
  pointing at an unpushed finish commit after a failed push: on push failure
  it is restored to `refs/remotes/origin/dev`.
- After the push, `finish` asserts its own commit (including any rebased
  replacement hash produced by non-fast-forward recovery) is an ancestor of
  the pushed `origin/dev` tip (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit>
  refs/remotes/origin/dev`) and fails loudly, naming the commit hash, when it
  is not; on refusal the worktree and feature branch are retained and the
  work item is not advanced to `in_review`.
- The safe-skip semantics of `_sync_parent_branch` are preserved: never
  force-update, never `reset --hard` the shared checkout, never lose local
  commits, never fail a finish that already pushed.
- The pre-push fast-forward property (pre-push context-budget gate measures
  the main checkout with the new files present) is preserved, ideally by
  wiring the verified sync so the gate sees the tree on `origin/dev`; the
  property stays explicitly under test (extend
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` /
  `tests/test_implement_push_*`).
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the
  dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation

- Restructure `phase_finish` Step 5: compute whether the child commit is an
  ancestor of `refs/remotes/origin/dev` before advancing local `dev`, and
  only then fast-forward — or fast-forward from the remote-tracking ref after
  the push and verify ancestry before moving (AC1). Remove the silent
  `except Exception` that disables the fast-forward and instead refuse loudly
  when local `dev` has moved.
- On push failure in Step 6 (including `PushTimeoutError` /
  `PushNonFastForwardError` paths that bail), restore local `dev` to
  `refs/remotes/origin/dev` so it never stays on the unpushed commit.
- Add the post-push ancestry assertion after Step 6 (and after the
  non-fast-forward recovery retry in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`,
  re-asserting with the rebased replacement hash), raising a named failure
  that reports the hash and leaves recoverable state.
- Extend the F1 sandbox tests with the ancestry and restore assertions; extend
  `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` to assert ancestry
  after the recovery rebase.

- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_finish_concurrent_orphan.py`
- `SorraAgents/tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py`

# Acquire child lock in phase_start; classify held children as skipped-held

## Summary
Wire the shared lock into `implement.py` at the single choke point `phase_start`
(as the first step after validation, before the claim and worktree create/resume),
propagate ownership to child/driver subprocesses, and report held children as
`skipped-held` in `phase_parent`/`phase_drive`. Satisfies AC-1, AC-3, AC-4, AC-6.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 1. `phase_start` acquires the child lock before the work-item claim and before any worktree creation/resume; a failed acquire aborts with a `skipped-held` report (holder identity populated) and performs no claim, no status/assignee mutation, no worktree create/remove and no file writes (AC-1).
- 2. The lock is held for `phase_start`'s lifetime and released on normal exit, exception/abort, and SIGINT/SIGTERM. On SIGTERM between the claim and worktree creation the lock is released and the child is left with an explanatory comment naming the interruption (asserted by a test) — never a claimed item with neither a worktree nor a comment (AC-3).
- 3. `_classify_child` maps a held child to `skipped-held`; `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` report `action: "skipped-held"` with `held_by: {agent, pid, session_id, started_at}` and stop cleanly instead of spawning a second session (AC-1).
- 4. Driver re-entrancy: the driver subprocess chain and driven child (running `start`/`finish` for the same child id) are not falsely blocked — ownership by explicit `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` propagated via `_child_session_env`/`_invoke_implement`, never pid heuristics (AC-4).
- 5. Existing guards preserved and not weakened: `skip-in-progress` classification, `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion refusal, worktree placement guard, stranded-child finalisation ownership check (AC-6).
- 6. Lock path resolves to `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` (worklog store), never inside the worktree; host-wide `process_semaphore` slot pools untouched.

- 7. **Parent AC4 — driver re-entrancy.** The driver's own subprocess chain and the driven child session it spawns (which runs `start`/`finish` for the same child id) are not falsely blocked: ownership is propagated by an explicit token (`IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, matching the token in the lock file) — never by "same pid" heuristics alone.
- 8. **Parent AC6 — scope discipline.** Existing guards are preserved and not weakened: `skip-in-progress` classification, `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion refusal, the worktree placement guard, and the stranded-child finalisation ownership check.

## Minimal Implementation
- `phase_start`: acquire lock first; wrap claim + worktree create/resume; release in `finally`/signal handler.
- `_child_session_env`/`_invoke_implement`: export `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` to spawned processes.
- `_classify_child` (+ `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` report assembly): `skipped-held` classification and holder fields; report surfaced via the existing JSON report conventions.

## Key Files
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start`, `_classify_child`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`, `_child_session_env`, `_invoke_implement`.
- `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py` — consumed (token API).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: shared lock module, unit tests, subprocess regression test.
- Lock module re-entrancy design must match AC-4.

## Deliverables
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` changes; unit + regression tests green.

# Temp-index staging in the finish gate

## Target outcome

Make the finish gate's test step validate the exact tree the commit will
produce: before the suite runs, copy the real index to a temporary file, apply
the change set to the copy (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`), and run the
suite with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported so every child `git` command (including
`git ls-files` inside tests) sees the staged file set. On success the real
index receives `git add -A` and the commit proceeds — after a `git write-tree`
equality assertion proving the committed tree is the tested tree. On failure
the temp index is deleted and the real index and working tree are untouched.

## Definition of done

- `phase_finish`'s test step creates the temp index and exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE`
  into the suite subprocess environment (reaching `git ls-files` and the cache
  fingerprint), using the F3-verified scrub pass-through.
- Success path: real `git add -A`, assert `git write-tree` of the real index
  equals the fingerprint the suite ran against, then commit; temp index removed.
- Failure/abort/exception paths: temp index removed, no commit, no residual
  staging — satisfying the F5 abort contract.
- No new bypasses (`TEST_SCOPE_SKIP` etc. absent); guard ownership

# implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps

`discovered-from:SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` — split out of the driven-session worktree-removal fix at producer request (Q2 of that item's intake). Same root cause, different caller: here the *session that invoked finish* is the operator's own agent session, not a driver-spawned child.

**Headline:** `implement.py finish` must not leave a plain leaf session unable to run any command: after finish removes the worktree, Pi's bash tool refuses every call in that session, so the report, the worklog comment and the post-push verification steps all fail.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` removes the worktree after the dev push (Step 7, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:5322`). In the plain leaf flow the finishing process is a **child** of the agent session (`bash` tool), and that session's cwd *is* the worktree. `_remove_worktree` chdirs only the finish process out of the tree (`:2364-2376`), so the session keeps a deleted cwd: Pi's bash tool then rejects every command with `Working directory does not exist: … / Cannot execute bash commands.` while absolute-path `read`/`write` still work. The session is reduced to a degraded loop exactly when it should be writing its completion comment, rendering its report and verifying the pushed commit.

## Users and user stories

- **Implement agent (plain leaf item)** — "As an agent finishing a leaf work item, I want my post-finish steps to run normally, so I do not have to invent absolute-path workarounds for the report and the post-push verification."
- **Operator / reviewer** — "As the reviewer, I want the session's final report and verification evidence produced by the workflow rather than improvised, so I can trust what I read."
- **Maintainer** — "As the maintainer, I want one deterministic rule for when a worktree may be deleted relative to the session that owns it."

## Recorded evidence

- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** (session `01a1840b-13a6-71a0-9153-f89e8dd2dfee`, TCE repo): the session hit `Working directory does not exist` **8 times** after its foreground `implement.py finish`, then worked around it — its own transcript notes "After that bash won't work, so do it last", and it removed a placeholder directory as its final action.
- Same failure mode documented in `SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR` for driven sessions (where it also wedges the drive loop); that item fixes the driven case only.

## Desired change (direction, not a fixed design)

The driven case is solved by deferring removal to the driver. The plain case has no external owner, so the options are:

1. **Defer to the session's own last step** — finish keeps the worktree and the implement skill's finish step ends with an explicit, runnable cleanup instruction (`git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`) that the *session* performs as its final action, after the comment, report and verification are done.
2. **Defer to a separate cleanup pass** — finish always defers; the cleanup skill / `implement.py` gains a `cleanup` action that removes worktrees of terminal items, run by the operator or the next workflow step.
3. **Make finish's removal non-fatal to the session** — keep removing, but ensure nothing after it needs bash (move report rendering/comment/verification *before* removal inside finish). Cheapest, but leaves the session's cwd dead for any later operator-driven interaction.

A design decision is required at intake/plan time; option 1 or 2 is expected to fit the existing `--keep-worktree` hatch added by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No dead cwd after finish in the plain flow.** A plain leaf session can still run bash commands after `implement.py finish` returns (or the workflow guarantees nothing after finish needs bash — depending on the chosen option), verified by a test that drives `phase_finish` and asserts the session-visible worktree state.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cleanup still happens deterministically.** Whichever option is chosen, a finished leaf item's worktree is removed by a named step within the same workflow run (session final action or cleanup pass), with the removal recorded in the finish/cleanup report.
- [ ] **AC3 — Consistency with the driven fix.** The mechanism reuses the deferral predicate/flag introduced by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR (`IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE`, `--keep-worktree` / `IMPLEMENT_KEEP_WORKTREE`) rather than adding a third removal path.
- [ ] **AC4 — Interruption safety.** An interrupted workflow leaves the worktree present and reported (never half-removed), and a repeat run is idempotent.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (finish step cleanup instructions), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` state the ownership rule for the plain flow.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation criterion.** New tests plus the changed-scope suite pass via the test skill (`/skill:test`), and the dev-push full-suite gate is green for the pushed commit.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the driven-session behaviour delivered by SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR; this item is the non-driven path only.
- Reuse `_remove_worktree`, `cleanup_worktree_processes` and the existing safety gates; no new deletion mechanism, no `rm -rf`-style shortcuts.
- Never remove a worktree that is dirty or whose item is non-terminal.
- Pi core's bash-tool behaviour on a missing cwd is out of scope (a Pi-core limitation, not fixable here).
- **Out of scope:** the pane transport, `hygiene_check.sh` rework, branch deletion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 6b/7 and the finish-step ordering, plus the deferral predicate shared with SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — finish-step cleanup instructions (currently a manual `git worktree remove` block, `SKILL.md:811`).
- `skill/implement/tests/` — extend the finish test harness (`test_finish_no_diff_status.py` style) for the plain-flow behaviour.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — ownership rule for the plain flow.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR** — "implement.py finish removes the worktree under a driven child session, wedging it" (open, parent of this split): fixes the driven path; this item must reuse its deferral mechanism.
- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** — finish SIGTERMing itself in `wl cleanup-worktree` (completed): the self-exclusion contract around Step 6b.
- **SA-0MRTSO5W8005ZGA7** — added the worktree process cleanup call to the workflow (completed).
- **RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33** — the plain-flow session that hit the deleted cwd 8 times (completed).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Options 1/2 leave worktrees behind on interruption** — mitigated by AC4 and by the cleanup skill.
- **Doc/instruction drift:** `SKILL.md` currently instructs the agent to run `git worktree remove` itself after pushing, duplicating finish's removal; the chosen option must make the instruction and the code agree.
- **Assumption:** the operator's session is the only other holder of the worktree cwd in the plain flow (no other process needs it), so removal timing is purely about the session's own remaining steps.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "just make Pi tolerate a deleted cwd" is a Pi-core change — record it, do not attempt it here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Scope split.** *Answer (producer, during SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR intake): "driver only, raise a follow up item for the plain leaf flow".* This item is that follow-up; the driven path is SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR.
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION, for planning) — Which cleanup owner for the plain flow?** (1) the session's own final step, (2) a separate cleanup pass, (3) move everything that needs bash before removal inside finish. Recommended: **(1)**, because it keeps a single workflow run responsible for its own cleanup and reuses the `--keep-worktree` hatch; (2) becomes preferable if the cleanup skill is the operator's normal sweep.
- **Q3 (answered by research) — Is the failure a hang?** No: bash is refused for the rest of the session while absolute-path file tools still work; the session degrades but does not block (RISE-0MVPZ31UJ000BC33's workaround).

- **SA-0MVJC5KNT0044L2B** – implement.py finish SIGTERMs itself in wl cleanup-worktree, stranding the dev push (completed)
- **SA-0MVMMHG9Z004F2ED** – implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root (open)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+267 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+253 more)

# Document and wire the plain-flow ownership rule in the implement skill and docs

Parent: **SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5** — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's cwd, breaking its post-finish steps*.

**Goal.** Make the plain leaf flow carry one unambiguous, machine-checked ownership rule: `finish <id> --keep-worktree` defers removal, and the session's **last** bash command (`implement.py cleanup <id>`) removes the tree — with no competing `git worktree remove` instruction left anywhere.

## Context

The parent's research found **doc/instruction drift**: `skill/implement/SKILL.md` currently tells the agent to run `git worktree remove .worklog/worktrees/… && git worktree prune && git checkout dev && git pull` *after* pushing, while `phase_finish` Step 7 removes the worktree itself. In the plain leaf flow this drift is the bug: either the instruction is skipped (finish already removed the tree, killing the session's cwd) or it is attempted from a dead cwd.

This child lands after the two code children (child 1: `cleanup` action; child 2: plain-flow deferral + report surface), so every instruction it writes is runnable.

The rule to state, once, in three places:

- **Plain leaf flow** — `implement.py finish <id> --keep-worktree`; the session finishes its comment, report and post-push verification; then, as its **last** bash command, `implement.py cleanup <id>`. After that command no bash works in the session (the cwd is gone by design).
- **Driven child flow** — unchanged: the session never removes its own worktree; `implement.py drive` removes it after the session exits (**SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR**).
- **Parent/parent-phase flow** — unchanged: `phase_parent` finishes children in its own subprocess and removes their worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Goal

Fix the shared post-remediation path so a passing-but-time-stale audit is resolved by content freshness instead of blocking the release with the contradictory reason `Ready to close`. The fix lives once in `attemptAuditRemediation()` and is consumed by the Step-2 audit gate, the Step-3.7 final-validation sweep and `refresh-audits.js` — no duplicated logic (parent AC2/AC3 implementation half).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC3: No contradictory block after in-gate remediation.
- Parent AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- `attemptAuditRemediation()` (in `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, ~line 643) accepts an injectable `queryContentFreshnessFn` defaulting to the real `queryContentFreshness()`; `check-final-validation.js` and `refresh-audits.js` pick up the fix from the shared function with no duplicated logic (only report wording may change in `check-final-validation.js`).
- Post-remediation status `{passing: true, stale: true}` with a v2 content fingerprint re-queries content freshness and: (a) fingerprint unchanged → returns `status: 'passing'` with a reason naming the content-fresh basis; (b) content changed / fingerprint-less / legacy / probe failure → returns `status: 'blocking'` with a reason naming `time-stale but content changed` plus the actionable remedy `audit_runner.py issue <id> --force`.
- No code path in either gate emits a blocking entry whose reason is `Ready to close` (the invariant test in the tests child stays green).
- Fail-open safety preserved: a probe failure falls back to the conservative time gate and still blocks — never silently passes a stale audit; `--force` appears only as the documented remedy, never in the happy path; `--skip-audit-remediation` semantics are unchanged; genuine fresh-failing, missing and content-changed audits still block.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate before any push to dev) (parent AC7).

## Constraints

- Scope discipline: the `audit_runner.py` `issue` short-circuit and the remediation budget are out of scope; record any runner improvements as separate work items.
- Shar the implementation: never duplicate the freshness logic in `check-final-validation.js` (parity principle — shared logic, not copies).
